title: Mastering Trend Following, Arbitrage, and Carry with J8 Capital - Open Interest 12

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Mastering Trend Following, Arbitrage, and Carry with J8 Capital - Open Interest 12.docx

speakers: Vishal (J8 head of trading and portfolio management)
summary: J8 Capital runs a decomposed multi-strategy program (trend in commodities, FX, bonds; curve arbitrage, FX carry, inventory, vol term structure) risk-weighted by inverse realised vol at 10 percent target. Redwood adds an intraday strategy with low correlation to CTA indices; costs are the key hurdle.

coverage.note: background of both guests, why systematic
GARS philosophy, decomposition into single return drivers
trend rules across markets, why no equities
equities exclusion, arbitrage and carry strategies
VIX term structure, risk allocation, target vol
leverage and margin, benchmark question, CTA nature

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: translate those into a systematic strategy allows to take out all the discretionary emotional behavioral Finance aspects
claims.claim: Translating economic fundamentals in commodities into rules-based strategies removes the emotional and behavioral biases of discretionary traders.
claims.testable: partly: compare rules vs discretionary results

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: you can also diversify AC cross model risk and if you if you wait the signals according to the risk assigned to a signal that you get an additional diversification boost
claims.claim: Beyond asset-class diversification, diversify across return drivers and models and weight signals by risk for an extra diversification gain.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: we decomposed all those different possible return drivers within the market create single strategy for each single return driver and risk component that we want to extract
claims.claim: Build one sub-strategy per return driver (e.g. commodity trend, term-structure arbitrage, inventory) then combine in a risk-based portfolio, instead of one big model with filters.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: instead of putting everything into one big modelist strategy where one may lose the oversight of where actually R return will dra on come from we decompose it
claims.claim: Decomposition keeps transparency on where returns come from and lets managers refine each risk driver separately.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: each single sub strategy that we construct therefore really consists of only one single uh degree of freedom
claims.claim: Each sub-strategy has one degree of freedom and simple parameters, so the overall product is complex but its parts are simple.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: each single Market has their own parameterization so we look at each markers individually
claims.claim: Same trend signal method across commodities, currencies and bonds but market-specific parameters.
claims.testable: yes: compare market-specific vs common parameters

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: it kicks in with returns and with with a hedge component where our long-term strategies may suffer draw Downs during reversal periods
claims.claim: A short-term momentum strategy hedges long-term trend drawdowns during reversals.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: you do have a survival bias within those indices which distorts let's say the long-term nature of a trend following approach
claims.claim: Equity indices have survival bias (losers removed) that truncates signals, so equities are excluded from long-term trend following.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: we want to avoid redundancy effects or resonance Effects by trading equities on top that will just be triggered by movements in the underly markets which we trade already anyways
claims.claim: Equities depend on rates, FX and commodity inputs already traded, so adding equity trend duplicates exposure.
claims.testable: partly: correlation of equity trend to other sleeves

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: whereas a commodity for example is uh a real input material into uh commod to into production into the economic uh life cycle so there's clear demand and Supply
claims.claim: Commodities have clear supply and demand fundamentals; shares are mainly speculative instruments once issued.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: in our long-term long-term uh slow momentum or Trend following approach um we did not find any added value by adding Equity indes to our PL
claims.claim: Adding equity index futures did not improve their long-term trend program.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: to profit from the RO yield differentials of the Futures along the term structure
claims.claim: Term-structure arbitrage harvests roll yield between long and short ends of the futures curve, closing the short end when the curve turns unsustainable.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: we reverse the trades when we observe a sell off in the market based on short-term realized volatility
claims.claim: FX carry (long high-yield, short low-yield vs USD) is reversed after a sell-off signalled by short-term realised volatility.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: going long the under supplied one and short the oversupplied one because you would expect an oversupplied Mar surprises to fall in under supplied Mar prices to increase
claims.claim: Commodity curvature indicates under- or oversupply; long undersupplied and short oversupplied commodities.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: inventory fundamental inory data that is often delayed and then also subject to Corrections
claims.claim: Use futures curve shape as a real-time inventory proxy because inventory data is delayed, revised and imprecise.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: you have annualized losses of around 50 60% per Anon which are purely Rong losses
claims.claim: Rolling front-month VIX futures loses about 50-60 percent a year from roll costs, so a short position can arbitrage it out.
claims.direction: short VIX front month via term structure

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: if you go short the FR month of volatility and then you see a 300% volatility spike in the DI can completely be catastrophic event to your entire portfolio
claims.claim: Short volatility carry has catastrophic tail risk in spikes, so it must be hedged and managed.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: if we simply take the inverse of the realized volatility of each of the systems and then and then uh weighted proportionately so essentially equal risk weighted uh asset allocation
claims.claim: Allocate across strategies by inverse realised volatility (equal risk), which gave the most stable overall return.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: the realized volatility between assets is fairly stable over time whereas of course um correlations or shortterm all performance of certain strategies
claims.claim: Realised volatility is stable while correlations and recent performance are unstable, so no correlation or performance tilts.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: we scale the exposure of our futures to achieve a realized Target volatility of 10%
claims.claim: Futures are unfunded, so scale exposure to a 10 percent target volatility (realised 10.26 percent over 10 years).

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: we just need to use between let's say six and 10 sometimes 12% margin Equity
claims.claim: At 10 percent target vol, margin to equity is about 6-12 percent, so 1 million cash controls roughly 30 million of notional.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: this index model broadly to let's say 80% of its returns broadly mimic or go or are similar to uh popular CTA Benchmark Ines
claims.claim: A simple index built from survey answers explained about 80 percent of CTA index returns: diversified, risk-weighted 12-month momentum.

claims.speaker: Tilman (J8 co-founder)
claims.quote: I would say we are 50% traditional CTA 50% % let's say alternative risk premium so CTA plus
claims.claim: J8 is half traditional CTA and half alternative risk premia, so no single benchmark fits.

claims.speaker: Vishal (J8, head of trading)
claims.quote: the base of the strategy is all about exploiting those extreme movements or not even extreme like I mean we talk in terms of like breakouts being measured in terms of volatility
claims.claim: Redwood trades intraday breakouts measured in volatility terms within trend, volatility and positioning context.

claims.speaker: Vishal (J8, head of trading)
claims.quote: this strategy is focused on the big futures the future which have good liquidity uh which are easy to get in and get out
claims.claim: Short-term trading requires highly liquid futures for cheap entry and exit.

claims.speaker: Vishal (J8, head of trading)
claims.quote: this correlation of the short-term strategy to any of the CDA indices uh available across the board whether to SNP individually or to other industry benchmarks is quite low in fact some of them are quite bit negative also
claims.claim: Short-term strategy has low or negative correlation to CTA indices and improved risk-adjusted return in simulations.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (host)
claims.quote: found it practically nothing it's like very close to 0
claims.claim: Redwood's correlation with the short-term traders index is near zero.

claims.speaker: Vishal (J8, head of trading)
claims.quote: my trend is defined in a slightly different way than the the long-term Trend
claims.claim: Short-term trading is not simply counter-trend; each strategy uses its own horizon context including volatility.

claims.speaker: Vishal (J8, head of trading)
claims.quote: 700 round trips uh per million per month
claims.claim: About 700 round trips per million per month (roughly 8,000 per year) across 12 futures.

claims.speaker: Vishal (J8, head of trading)
claims.quote: the real challenge in the short shortterm stuff is to avoid whiplashes because there's a lot of noise in the short-term space
claims.claim: Short-term systems get higher Sharpe at similar returns but must avoid whipsaws from noise.

claims.speaker: Vishal (J8, head of trading)
claims.quote: it's not anything substantial to say that the strategy is impacted by slightly varing um transaction cost
claims.claim: Vishal says performance is not highly sensitive to small cost changes; he lacks exact numbers.

claims.speaker: Moritz Seibert (host)
claims.quote: when we do these 8 8,000 round turns per million per year you're down about 11% uh 10.8% to be exact in terms of uh expected execution and implementation cost
claims.claim: Moritz's math: at about 6 dollars per contract and 8,000 round turns per million, costs are about 10.8 percent a year, a very high hurdle for short-term strategies.

claims.speaker: Vishal (J8, head of trading)
claims.quote: you can easily do overtrading in the short-term space
claims.claim: Short-term systems can easily overtrade, so exposure and sensitivity must be controlled.

claims.speaker: Vishal (J8, head of trading)
claims.quote: we have built our own in-house uh infrastructure for the fix uh execution
claims.claim: Intraday trading needs 24-hour automated infrastructure (FIX execution, alerts, monitoring desks in India and UK), an operational overhead.
